label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.

findings.quote: the nine, greyed. Each lights for a moment
findings.why: Starting the tour, I do not yet know who the nine are or why they light; the cast is named only in chapters I may not have read.
An instruction on how to read; the dramatised note could simply be said in the editor's voice, as what I did.

findings.quote: The line on the slide matters: the map shows where things sit relative to each other.
findings.why: The figure line already carries 'positions, not measurements', so this tells the same thing a second time and tells me it matters.

findings.quote: The home page says the perfect storm.
findings.why: The phrase 'perfect storm' is used before I am told what the storm is, and the three circles are explained only in the next stop.

findings.quote: The team, as the site shows it: who does what
findings.why: A narrator line that reports the page with no 'I' and no hindsight; what the editor made of the roll call is missing.

findings.quote: The point is the receipt at the end of each: every decision leaves a record.
findings.why: The agent's line, 'Allowed, denied, or asked. Never silent.', says the same thing straight after, and 'the point is' is the opening the book avoids.

findings.quote: The first walks the night hour by hour. The second is the talk as I gave it.
findings.why: Short sentences in a run with stops 10 and 11 that all end on a one-line agent quip; the stops read as a repeating template.

findings.quote: That is what one day made.
findings.why: A closing line of the 'that is the point' family, after thirteen stops that already said it.

findings.quote: it may be worth asking an agent to build the next one the same way
findings.why: As a newsroom builder I want one concrete thing to copy, and this is vague; the roll call page or the receipt is the thing I would try first.

findings.quote: like deck's, still open when the hold came
findings.why: A glossary entry leans on 'deck', a member I have not met if I jumped here, so the definition does not stand alone.

findings.quote: hour one runs from midnight to a minute before one, and the talk was due as hour nineteen ended
findings.why: A story detail in a glossary line; a word box should only define the clock.

findings.quote: The difference is the book's point.
findings.why: It ranks the idea for me instead of letting the next sentence carry it; the sentence after it is the strong one.

findings.quote: as the team's own slide said
findings.why: A reference to a slide I have not seen inside a table cell.

findings.quote: that same evening the usage limit came before any hold did
findings.why: The 'usage limit' is not explained in this appendix and the cell is cryptic for a reader who skipped the chapter.

findings.quote: four refused, one failed because the session did not exist, one probably refused or never sent
findings.why: The longest cell packs six outcomes and the term 'review steps' without a plain account of what they were trying to reach.

what_holds: 90-the-tour-at-length.md: the policy review page and the one-action journey (allowed, denied, asked, never silent) are things I could rebuild for my own newsroom.
91-the-words-used.md: short plain definitions with the chapter named; I can look a word up and go back.
93-appendix-b-the-control-register.md: the setting versus expectation split and the 'what it missed' column are the honest answer I want; this is the most useful of the three for an editor who signs.
notes: Read as a five-minute reader. The tour is pleasant but repeats one shape thirteen times; the register is the section I would keep open while setting up my own agents.
